newsitem.title: USA: CME Dec hog futures end limit up, post new high.
newsitem.headline: CME Dec hog futures end limit up, post new high.

text.p: CME December hog futures ran up the 1.500 cent per lb daily limit at the close and set a new contract high while pork bellies posted a limit gain of 3.000 cents in February's closing range as rising cash belly prices sparked strong demand, traders said.

December hogs set a new high of 58.825 cents a lb at its limit up close while other months ended mostly 1.050 to 0.250 higher. February pork bellies settled 2.975 higher at 76.800 cents. Other belly contracts ended up 2.875 to 2.400 cents.
Both pits rose on strong demand linked to this week's light hog runs and firmer cash pork prices, traders said.

"Cash hogs just haven't moved and we saw cash hog prices firm up as the day wore on. The big thrust there (in futures) is the anticipation that we are going to have much better pork prices after the Thanksgiving holiday, and seasonally, that is a good demand time" by consumers, said Paul Georgy, president of advisory group, Allendale Inc.
Traders said packers were paying up for hogs despite saying they were cutting back on the rate of hog slaughter due to poor margins, but the real reason is likely the tight supply of hogs.
"Packers just can't get the hogs," one trader said.

Georgy also noted that normally the expiring hog contract month has shown longs in control and shorts have to cover their positions. It is a pattern that has happened in the old live contract and should not be a factor in the new lean contract, he added.

Wholesale pork prices also showed renewed strength in most cuts Thursday after some weakness Wednesday. This accounted for much of the runup in pork belly futures to one-month highs and a limit gain for February in the closing range, traders said.
"It's a cash and technical rally," said Mark Palmer, independent pork belly trader.
Palmer said February could go up to 79.000 cents on the charts.
Traders relayed talk that fresh bellies had sold at $70 per cwt for next week delivery, which would put cash prices at best levels since October 8.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture quoted 14-16 lb cash bellies at $67 early Thursday, the highest documented price since October 10.
Rand Financials and E.D.&F. Man notably bought both hog and belly futures.
In hog options, locals bought calls and sold puts on the rally in futures, pit sources added.
